$comment: PINNED SCREEN PARAMETERS. Written before the screen was run against any stranger wallet.
Every number here is anchored to a measurement that already exists in this repository or in
a committed scout report, and the anchor is named in `justification`. Do not move a value to
fit an output. If a value must change, change it here, say why in the PR, and re-run Stage 0
first: a screen that no longer reproduces the one answer we already know is not ready to
judge strangers. tools/deployer-screen/SCREEN.md is the long-form version of this file.
Keyed, MadeOnSol, one request per candidate. A GATE, not a score: it asks whether a
deployer is competent, which is necessary and nowhere near sufficient. The denominator is
`profile.pump_tokens[].complete` and nothing else — never `bonding_rate`, `total_bonded`,
`total_tokens_deployed`, `recent_bond_rate`, `recent_outcomes` or `best_token_peak_mc`, all
of which are trailing windows or stale, and never /deployer-hunter/{wallet}/tokens, which
is bonded-only and so has no denominator at all.

justification.minTokens: MadeOnSol's own spec tells consumers to gate on labeled_tokens >= 3. That is far too low: on our subject deployer a 22-token window read 0.6818 against a true 0.4310, so a window of ~22 was enough to be wrong by 58% relative. 25 is the floor at which the vendor's own sliding-window artefact stops being the whole measurement, and it is 8x their published gate. It is NOT enough for a lifetime claim, which is why the rate is a gate and the span is reported.
justification.minCompletionRate: 0.25 is MadeOnSol's own published 'good' tier lifetime bar. Our subject deployer's true lifetime rate is 0.4310 (239 launches, 103 bonded) and it is a genuinely competent operator, so a bar meaningfully below that admits the population we care about while excluding deployers that mostly fail.
justification.minSpanDays: A high rate earned inside a single day is a burst, not a record. 14 days is the shortest span over which pump.fun's own time-to-bond distribution puts a majority of eventual graduations behind us: on our tape 82.5% of graduations occur within 7 days and 85.4% within 14.

$comment: Keyless, pump.fun, the actual recommendation. Reproduces the method of
data/slot-zero-june-regime-change/report.md §5.1: the operation's share of the curve's
bottom = (dev buy + co-ordinated stake) / (dev buy + all create-slot stake). Co-ordination
is detected structurally, not from any wallet list: a single transaction carrying two or
more distinct swapping wallets is a bundle, and independent traders cannot share a
transaction. Verified to recover our subject's known six-wallet cohort without being told
who it is — see SCREEN.md, Stage 0.
stage2_score.coordinationRule: a create-slot transaction carrying >= 2 distinct swapping wallets marks every wallet in it as co-ordinated

justification.minRoomLeft: Anchored on the only regime this project has ever MEASURED as profitable for create-slot outsiders. June report §5.1: operation share was 0.451 before 2026-06-04 (room 0.549) and 0.768 after (room 0.232). §6.1: outsiders in the create slot took +6.54 SOL per launch before, +1.79 after, and outsiders entering later went from +5.43 to -0.74. So room >= 0.55 is the pre-step regime and nothing tighter has ever been observed to pay. This threshold deliberately REJECTS our own subject deployer, which is the point of Stage 0.
justification.minLaunchesSampled: 8 launches is the smallest sample whose median is not one launch's accident, at a per-launch cost of 1-3 keyless requests. Below 8 the candidate is reported as UNSCORED rather than scored, because a thin median here would be read as a recommendation.
justification.maxLaunchesSampled: 12 caps the keyless spend per candidate. The June report measured sustainable keyless pacing at roughly 0.5 requests/second with one request in flight; 12 launches x up to 3 pages is ~36 requests, about 70 seconds per candidate.

$comment: The captain's word was 'consistently'. MadeOnSol cannot answer it: their only
denominator-complete surface (profile.pump_tokens) is capped at 70 records and about 35
days. Manufacturing a long-horizon claim from a 35-day window is exactly the defect we
found in their own aggregate, so the tool does not do it. Long-horizon consistency is
reported as UNMEASURED unless --consistency is passed, which runs a keyless pump.fun
creator walk on stage-2 survivors only.

justification.epochDays: 30-day epochs are long enough that a prolific deployer's epoch is not one week of luck and short enough that a 6-month history yields the 3 epochs required.
justification.maxDispersion: max(epoch rate) - min(epoch rate) > 0.35 flags a deployer as STREAKY rather than excluding it. A flag, not a filter: the whole point of the exercise is that one hot window must not read as a record, and the reader is entitled to see the spread rather than have it silently applied.

$comment: Hard bounds. The key is the captain's own and its Free-tier allowance (about 200
requests/day, 10/minute) is SHARED. Every ceiling here is enforced in code, and there is no
flag that disables one.

justification.maxKeyedRequests: Enumeration costs 3 (one leaderboard page per sort key) and the gate costs 1 per candidate, so 20 candidates cost 23. The 45 ceiling leaves headroom for a retry and a second enumeration page while staying under a quarter of the shared daily allowance.
justification.keyedMinIntervalMs: Free tier bursts at ~10/minute. 6.5s between request starts keeps a run under that with margin, and margin matters because the allowance is shared with whatever else holds this key.
justification.keylessMinIntervalMs: The June report measured sustainable keyless pump.fun pacing at ~0.5 requests/second with one request in flight; batching and concurrency were both measured harmful. 2000ms is that pacing with margin.
